chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ إِشْكَيْبَ، عَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ الْبَرْقِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ وَأَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ قَالَا

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Al-Husayn ibn Ishkib, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Abi al-Abbas who said:

chunks.arabic_text: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ إِذَا أَبُو بَصِيرٍ دَخَلَ، فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يُقْدِمْ أَحَدًا يَشْكُو أَصْحَانَا الْعَامَ، قَالَ هِشَامٌ: فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ يَعْرِضُ بِأَبِي بَصِيرٍ

translations.en: We were together with Abi Abdillah when Abu Basir entered, so Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: All praise be to Allah who did not bring forth anyone who complains about our companions this year. Hisham said: I thought that he was alluding to Abu Basir.

en.summary: This brief narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the dynamic between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his companions, specifically illustrating the subtle social cues used to address individual behavior within the community. Hisham ibn Salim’s immediate inference that Abu Basir was the subject of the Imam’s praise underscores the high level of attentiveness and intimacy among the close circle of the Imam’s followers. This incident serves as a key example of how the Imams managed the reputations and conduct of their companions with gentle, indirect guidance rather than public rebuke.
en.seo_question: Why did Hisham ibn Salim think Imam al-Sadiq was alluding to Abu Basir?
